=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1325-1334
  Problem: `REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT` accepts arbitrarily large numeric values without an upper bound.
  Why it fails at runtime: The shell arithmetic check (`[[ "$REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT" -gt 0 ]`) validates that the value is a positive integer but does not enforce a maximum. An operator (or misconfigured repo variable) setting `REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT=99999` would cause the wait loop to defer stall decisions for ~69 days, effectively disabling stall detection entirely and masking genuinely hung review runs. This is a configuration guardrail gap — not an external attacker vector — but the same class of operator error that the run's own comment warns about ("a 30 here would override the downstream 40 default and re-introduce the wait-review false-timeout").
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1578-1591, 1773-1786 (three sites)
  Problem: The jq `test("...")` function performs case-sensitive matching. The literal `claude-branch-review` in the pattern requires the job name to contain exactly that lowercase string. If a future variant of the wrapper workflow or GitHub Actions generates a job name with a different casing — e.g. `(Claude-branch-review)` with capital C, or a future `(pr-reviewer-pass-2)` suffix not present in the current pattern — the selector chain falls through to `jobs[0]` and the original bug (wrong job selected) resurfaces silently.
  Why it fails at runtime: In wrapper runs, `jobs[0]` is the completed gate job (~4s) whose log never grows during reviewer/editor work. The activity signal (`log_sz`) and early-exit shortcuts (`editor-noop`, `reviewer-majority`) would remain inert, and if the stall timer fires, the wait loop would still give up on a healthy long reviewer step — the exact regression this PR was supposed to prevent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1578-1591
  Problem: The jq regex pattern for selecting the codex-agent job uses a bounded suffix pattern that may not match all wrapper workflow job-name variations.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the regex fails to match the intended job due to an unanticipated job name variation, both the live-log shortcut and the activity signal would remain inert, causing the wait loop to time out even though the review run completed successfully.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
